llm.reply:
The KRAS gene product is a small GTPase [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. Its OMIM entry is titled KRAS PROTOONCOGENE, GTPase; KRAS [4]. Activating mutations turn it into a transforming oncoprotein [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"].

## GTPase Regulation

KRAS activity is promoted by an upstream guanine nucleotide exchange factor [28: "the cognate guanosine exchange factor (GEF) Son of Sevenless 1 that drives KRAS"]. Inhibiting this exchange factor has been proposed as an indirect way to target KRAS mutants that lack direct inhibitors [28: "The other KRAS mutations may be targeted indirectly via inhibition of the cognate guanosine exchange factor (GEF) Son of Sevenless 1"].

## Downstream Signaling

KRAS-dependent gene transcription runs mainly through the ERK MAPK pathway [29: "is driven predominantly through the ERK mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascade"]. ERK signaling downstream of KRAS deregulates cell-cycle machinery that drives tumor growth [29: "ERK deregulation of the anaphase promoting complex/cyclosome (APC/C) and other components of the cell cycle machinery"].

## Oncogenic Consequences

The mutant protein is implicated in several cancers [11: "implicated in various malignancies, including lung adenocarcinoma, mucinous adenoma, ductal carcinoma of the pancreas and colorectal carcinoma"]. Beyond G12C covalent inhibitors, degrading KRAS gave stronger pathway suppression than inhibiting it [30: "KRAS degradation results in more profound and sustained pathway modulation across a broad range of KRAS mutant cell lines"].

The KRAS gene product belongs to the small GTPase superfamily [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. The OMIM record for the gene is titled KRAS PROTOONCOGENE, GTPase; KRAS [4]. A single amino acid substitution activates the protein, and the resulting transforming protein is implicated in several cancers [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation"].

## Gene Identity

The gene symbol is KRAS [1]. The gene name is KRAS [5]. PubTator3 lists the literature entity name Kras [6]. Alternative splicing produces two isoforms that differ at the C-terminus [11: "variants encoding two isoforms that differ in the C-terminal region"].

## Signaling and Oncogenesis

KRAS-dependent transcription in mutant cancers runs mainly through ERK signaling [29: "is driven predominantly through the ERK mitogen-activated protein kinase (MAPK) cascade"]. Mutant KRAS activates TFCP2, which reprograms fibroblasts into lipid-rich cells that promote angiogenesis [27: "KRAS* activates the transcription factor CP2 (TFCP2)"]. One study title is Oncogenic KRAS Drives Lipofibrogenesis to Promote Angiogenesis and Colon Cancer Progression. [9]. Another study title is Defining the KRAS- and ERK-dependent transcriptome in KRAS-mutant cancers. [18].

## Therapeutic Targeting

KRAS was long considered undruggable, but G12C inhibitors have now reached the clinic [26: "AMG510 was the first drug-targeting KRAS (G12C) to be approved for clinical use"]. One review is titled KRAS mutation: from undruggable to druggable in cancer. [2]. Another review is titled Targeting KRAS in pancreatic cancer. [14]. In pancreatic cancer, the common mutations are not G12C [28: "G12D (44%), G12V (34%) and G12R (20%)"]. A heterobifunctional degrader breaks down most of the prevalent oncogenic alleles [30: "potently degrades 13 out of 17 of the most prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles"]. That work is titled Targeting cancer with small-molecule pan-KRAS degraders. [22].

The related records include the publication PMID 34776511 [8]. They also include PMID 37768068 [13]. They also include PMID 38686056 [17]. They also include PMID 38843331 [21]. They also include PMID 39298590 [25].

## Variants and Trials

ClinVar lists NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.458ATG[1] (p.Asp154del) [3]. ClinVar lists NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.36T>C (p.Gly12=) [10]. ClinVar lists NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.337C>T (p.Leu113=) [15]. ClinVar lists NM_033360.4(KRAS):c.524A>G (p.Glu175Gly) [19]. ClinVar lists NM_004985.5(KRAS):c.417T>A (p.Ile139=) [23].

One trial is Sorafenib in Combination With Irinotecan in Metastatic Colorectal Cancer Patients With KRAS Mutated Tumors [7]. Another is PREMIUM, Observational Study [12]. Another is A Trial of mFOLFIRI With MEK162 in Patients With Advanced RAS (HRAS, NRAS, or KRAS) Positive Metastatic Colorectal Cancers [16]. Another is Frequency of EGFR and KRAS Mutations and Clinical-prognostic Correlation in Brazilian Lung Cancer Patients [20]. Another is A Phase 1/2, Study Evaluating the Safety, Tolerability, PK, and Efficacy of Sotorasib (AMG 510) in Subjects With Solid Tumors With a Specific KRAS Mutation (CodeBreaK 100) [24].
